newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian penis-shrinker death toll hit seven.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian penis-shrinker death toll hit seven.

text.p: Seven men have been beaten and burnt to death in Ivory Coast's commercial capital Abidjan by angry mobs accusing them of being penis-shrinking sorcerers, police said on Monday.

The dead included two Ivorians and five African migrants from the West African nation's neighbours, they added. They were killed in Abidjan's populous districts and suburbs between Thursday and Saturday night.
State radio and television have broadcast appeals for calm.
Interior Minister Emile Constant Bombet, interviewed on Friday's main evening television news, appealed for calm, telling Ivorians that the problem existed only in their minds.
"I appeal once again for understanding on all sides so that our brothers who have chosen to live in harmony with us in this country are at no time troubled (by such incidents)," he said.
"Openness has long been Ivory Coast's policy."
Bombet said such attacks threatened to harm Ivory Coast's image in the world and compromise its reputation as a nation promoting peace and stability, needed for foreign investment.

Such reports are not uncommon in West or Central Africa. Purported victims often blame handshakes with sorcerers. At least 12 men were killed in Ghana in January by mobs accusing them of making penises shrink or vanish.

Police in Ghana and Ivory Coast dismiss the phenomenon as a ploy by thieves to cause a crowd to form and then rob people. Some victims say sorcerers touch them and make their penises shrink or vanish to extort cash in return for a cure.
